channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal trade sustains burners as tree loss threatens food security
item.description: A government energy compact says 36% of people have electricity access and only 15% have access to clean cooking.

item.title: Sierra Leone finance minister faces civil-society call for dismissal
item.description: The CSOs Consortium on Public Accountability says Sheku Bangura should be removed, while a guest writer defends his record on inflation and debt.

item.title: Analyst asks whether Sierra Leone's vice presidency is a dead end
item.description: Foday M. Daboh, a public policy analyst, argues that vice presidents have rarely been groomed as successors and often enter office without an independent political base.

item.title: Cape Verde raises benchmark rate to 2.75%
item.description: The central bank lifted its benchmark by 25 basis points from 16 November, citing inflation pressures and the risk of foreign-currency outflows.

item.title: French frigate visits Dar es Salaam to deepen maritime cooperation
item.description: The Nivôse arrived on 17 November after more than three years, with surveillance equipment and an 85-sailor crew.

item.title: Mali parliament approves 43 million euros for 144 communes
item.description: The funding will support water, health care, education and farming and pastoral activities in six central and northern regions through June 2028.

item.title: MTN Rwanda reports Rwf167.5 billion in first-half service revenue
item.description: The operator had 8.7 million subscribers by the end of June, as active data and Mobile Money users also increased.

item.title: Malawi’s plastic waste reaches 75,000 tonnes a year, report estimates
item.description: A 2021 estimate put about 80% of the country’s plastic waste in single-use plastics, amid concern over disposal along the Lilongwe-Kasungu road.

item.title: Mauritius records 27 947 road offences in nine months
item.description: The third Penalty Point System review lists speeding and seat-belt violations among the most common offences recorded through 31 October 2026.

item.title: Newsfile weighs University of Ghana hostel fees, detention directive and $60.68 million...
item.description: The programme will examine Rent Control's order on unassessed rent increases alongside the government's case for replacing its ageing presidential aircraft.

item.title: Tunisia lists 11,271 state properties, targets full inventory by 2030
item.description: The state property minister says the register will support better protection and management, while legal disputes complicate the status of some land.

item.title: Petro Ivoire launches PI Auto Services to take over Fix N’Go work
item.description: The new subsidiary follows Petro Ivoire’s acquisition of Point S and will provide vehicle servicing and maintenance in Côte d’Ivoire.

item.title: Algeria sets rural housing aid at 1.1 million dinars for mountain communes
item.description: Housing Minister Mohamed Tarek Belaribi says a decree listing eligible communes is imminent, following the increase from 700,000 dinars.

item.title: Ivorian doctors’ leader urges African health sovereignty at Dakhla summit
item.description: Aboubacar Sidiick Bakayoko called for partnerships to give African health workers placements and skills training at advanced simulation centres.

item.title: ACCA Uganda urges accountants to tackle stigma and prepare sustainability data
item.description: At its Kampala convention, the association called for earlier environmental data collection as Uganda plans a phased rollout of international reporting standards.

item.title: Guinea minister cites child protection and service gaps
item.description: At the 20 November ceremony in Conakry, Aminata Kaba named violence, female genital mutilation and child labour among persistent challenges.

item.title: Somalia's opposition rejects president's offer of election talks
item.description: The leaders turned down a meeting at the president's proposal, saying the election model must be reversed before any engagement, while the Constitutional Court has ordered.

item.title: Lagos opens 294 homes and targets 2,000 more by 2027
item.description: Two-bedroom terrace homes at Treasure Estate are priced at N65 million, with mortgage finance available through federal lenders.

item.title: Ethiopia conflict displaces about 700,000 as fighting spreads 300 kilometres
item.description: Islamic Relief says clashes over control of Moyale have damaged homes and businesses and disrupted health, water and sanitation services.

item.title: South Africa mourns former deputy president Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka
item.description: The country’s first female deputy president died on Friday at 71; the University of Johannesburg and political leaders paid tribute.

item.title: Tunisia's training system faces a skills mismatch as AI reshapes work
item.description: Degrees alone no longer guarantee lasting employment as AI automates writing, research, programming and data analysis, an article argues.

item.title: New Birth Association recreates old Tripoli home at Benghazi heritage event
item.description: The charity’s booth displays traditional architecture and household objects as part of Heritage Nights, organised by the Libyan Heritage and Wildlife Authority.

item.title: Madagascar court moves Ambohimalaza poisoning trial toward former health minister
item.description: Lawyers for the civil parties want the former health minister, doctors and gendarmes called as witnesses over the response to the poisoning that killed at least 35 people.

item.title: Kenya's electoral commission invites parties to submit 2027 poll reforms
item.description: The invitation followed an opposition walkout from a Nairobi consultation before the commission presented its election-preparedness plans.

item.title: DR Congo health professionals warn against antibiotic misuse
item.description: The advice comes during a Kinshasa campaign running from 18 to 24 November on antimicrobial resistance in people and animals.

item.title: Tunisia plans 2027 export programmes for olive oil, dates and handicrafts
item.description: Trade Minister Samir Abid also outlined a plan to promote Tunisian olive oil in the United States, Canada and some Asian markets.

item.title: Malawi committee considers inquiry into forfeited assets
item.description: The proposed inquiry would examine delays in disposing of seized properties, including Paul Mphwiyo’s K690 million house in Lilongwe.

item.title: Uganda gives Vitol 10-year mandate to market Pearl Sweet crude
item.description: The international trader will seek buyers and competitive prices, while Uganda National Oil Company retains oversight of each sale.

item.title: Soludo approves N50,000 December bonus for Anambra workers
item.description: The governor said the payment is expected in December 2026 salaries and ordered secretariat road repairs, an ICT centre and tree pruning.

item.title: Steinmeier and Ruto to discuss trade and migration in Nairobi
item.description: The German president visits Kenya from November 24 to 26 with a business delegation as the two countries review cooperation.

item.title: Burundi researcher explains how earthworms turn farm waste into compost
item.description: Eric Kazitsa says the process uses agricultural and food-processing residues, with earthworms producing more than 20 offspring monthly when well raised.

item.title: Port-Louis Waterfront festival caps dishes at Rs 275
item.description: More than 30 food stands are part of the second edition, with concerts and DJ sets scheduled from 19 h to 21 h on Saturday and Sunday.

item.title: Donors pledge $221 million to Malawi recovery projects
item.description: The World Bank expects the money to flow within days of agreements signed in Lilongwe, despite persistent fuel and foreign-exchange shortages.

item.title: Treasury audits Egenco’s K2.62 billion debt-recovery fee
item.description: Egenco paid M&M Global Law Consultants 15% of money recovered from Escom, and the Treasury ordered linked accounts frozen during the audit.

item.title: Uganda suspends mass gatherings in 34 Ebola-risk border districts
item.description: Concerts, festivals and rallies require written Health Ministry clearance as authorities tighten controls on movement across the border with the DRC.

item.title: Madagascar civil society groups prepare joint statement on election process
item.description: The planned declaration would challenge the conduct of the 9 and 10 November electoral consultations at the Ivato International Conference Centre.

item.title: World Bank report warns Malawi firms face a $4 trillion credit gap
item.description: The global shortfall affects micro, small and medium enterprises, while Malawi’s private-sector credit growth fell to 23.7% in August.

item.title: Germany offers Madagascar €56.5 million in development grants
item.description: The funding includes €46.4 million for financial cooperation and €10.1 million for technical support across several sectors.

item.title: French and Malagasy business groups discuss urban water and waste services
item.description: MEDEF International and Madagascar's business group met government officials in Antananarivo on water, sanitation and waste management as French lawmaker Bruno Fuchs held.

item.title: Dangote lifts daily petrol supply to 31.89 million litres as imports climb
item.description: Nigeria brought in 15 million litres of petrol a day in October, even as the country's largest refinery raised its own output by 12%.

item.title: Eswatini utility projects 200-unit power bills rising to E819 by 2028/29
item.description: The proposed two-year increases would lift a household’s monthly bill from E572, while new local power plants are not expected to cut prices immediately.

item.title: Betterland Ghana spends GH¢500,000 renovating Gwira Banso police station
item.description: The mining company funded accommodation, repairs and electrical work at the facility in Nzema East Municipality, in Ghana's Western Region.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea orders design talks for five proposed cultural sites
item.description: South Korea's TAEIN Development, an architectural firm, presented plans for museums in three cities and cultural centres in Annobón and Ciudad de La Paz.

item.title: Zinder women's groups launch drive for Niger's solidarity fund
item.description: The Mata Massu Doubara ambassadors held the launch on Friday, answering the president's call for CFA100 per person.

item.title: Smart Energy and CTCI sign financing-backed solar deal for Alépé factory
item.description: The project combines nearly 1.5 megawatt-peak of solar panels with 2 megawatt-hours of storage to address power cuts and voltage drops.

item.title: Niger's football federation draws 36 clubs into national cup
item.description: The preliminary stage opens with 18 ties, and 16 clubs will join the Super League teams in the last 16 after a fresh draw.

item.title: Ouaddaï agencies train about 50 young people in digital skills
item.description: The four-day course in Abéché covers computing, artificial intelligence and responsible use of social media.

item.title: Sarjo Mballow Barrow links Bafuloto development to third-term vote
item.description: The Second Lady told residents their development requests would be met if Adama Barrow wins the December 5 presidential election.

item.title: Chad launches housing plan as N'Djamena adds 20 000 households a year
item.description: The government's new programme targets homes and serviced plots, while the ministry says it will stop allocating undeveloped land.

item.title: Kinshasa police detain three officers over road conduct
item.description: The provincial police chief ordered the detentions during checks on unauthorised flashing lights and other vehicle lighting in the capital.

item.title: ECOWAS ministers weigh host for ECO central bank in Abidjan
item.description: The ministers are also considering payment-system components and a transition framework for a gradual launch of the single currency in 2027.

item.title: Libya and US discuss trade council plan and market-entry obstacles
item.description: Officials reviewed the Trade and Investment Framework Agreement and ways to ease American companies’ entry into Libya’s market.

item.title: Libya launches U.S. partnership programme covering oil, energy and transport
item.description: The plan also includes mining, infrastructure investment and technology transfer, while the Libyan delegation is due to seek agreements and implementation timelines.

item.title: Chad's prime minister faces parliamentary questioning on 30 November
item.description: Deputy Mahamat Ahmat Lazina initiated the plenary-session questioning, whose official subject has not yet been announced.

item.title: Mondlane denies inciting violence as prosecutors question him
item.description: The opposition leader acknowledged calling demonstrations after Mozambique's disputed 2024 elections but said his appeal to supporters was a political metaphor.

item.title: Indalo plans R2.5 billion, 35-storey Cape Town development
item.description: ThirtyFour18 will include a five-star hotel, 101 apartments and office space, with construction scheduled to begin in April 2027 subject to approvals.

item.title: South African court pushes Kemi Seba extradition hearing to February 2027
item.description: The Pretoria hearing on Benin's request was postponed again, and Seba remains in detention in South Africa.

item.title: Gaye urges Lower Saloum voters to back Darboe over Barrow
item.description: The former MP says Kaur’s groundnut depot now employs fewer than five people, down from more than 100 during the trading season.

item.title: Morocco secures Norway carbon-credit deal for renewable energy
item.description: Norway will buy credits for up to 8.78 million tons of verified emission reductions from Moroccan projects between 2027 and 2036.

item.title: Angolan historian challenges 400-year account of Portuguese rule
item.description: José Bento Duarte says Portuguese presence across Angola did not amount to effective colonial control over most people and regions for centuries.

item.title: Libyan Iron and Steel links rising rebar prices to its production halt
item.description: The company says it is working to increase the quantities of rebar available in the local market, which it hopes will bring prices back to stability.

item.title: Chad group launches CFA155.56 million drive to revive science classes in Wadi Fira
item.description: The three-year programme targets teacher shortages and the lack of science streams, with CFA46.75 million allocated for 2026-2027.

item.title: Cameroon's deposits fund gives Afriland eight days to pay CFA141.96 billion
item.description: The demand covers principal, interest and penalties tied to a dispute involving MTN Cameroon and companies linked to businessman Baba Ahmadou Danpullo.

item.title: Guinea weather alert warns of heat through Nov. 25
item.description: Moderate to locally strong heat is forecast in Basse-Guinée and Forest Guinea, with high temperatures expected to persist at night.

item.title: Melikechi's autobiography traces his path from Thénia to Mars research
item.description: The book by physicist Noureddine Melikechi recounts his studies, research and move from Algeria to the United Kingdom in 1980.

item.title: Founding Alliance claims control of five Blue Nile areas and captures troops
item.description: The group said it seized 27 vehicles and six tanks; the state government says the army is working to restore security.

item.title: Upper West declares 938 of 1,167 communities free of open defecation
item.description: The regional share has risen from about 29% in 2011 to 79%, while Nandom's chief promises education across 88 communities.

item.title: Mali's transition council ratifies Aoua Keïta centre's new status
item.description: The change gives the women's vocational training centre administrative and financial autonomy through a board, directorate and scientific committee.

item.title: Senegalese journalist Bada Mbathie wins continental local-governance prize
item.description: The Le Soleil reporter was honoured for a story on young residents cleaning Thiaroye Kaw, where their association says members fund its equipment.

item.title: Saudi firm proposes 1,000,000-ton tank farm in Sierra Leone
item.description: AHQ says ARAMCO and ADNOC would supply feedstock, while Sierra Leone’s regulator has offered licensing and technical guidance.

item.title: Flamme Olympique holds Ligue 2 leader Satellite FC to 1-1
item.description: Mohamed Yattara equalised in the 59th minute, leaving Satellite level with Séquence FC on 24 points at the halfway stage.

item.title: Eswatini sends Zulu to Cairo Games planning seminar
item.description: The chef de mission is receiving updates on qualification, athlete services and preparations for the 2027 African Games in Egypt.

item.title: Chad names Daouda Ahmat Mahamat to head N'Djaména university
item.description: A 20 November presidential decree installs the professor in place of Mahamat Saleh Daoussa Haggar, who was suspended from the post.

item.title: SCR Maya brings in Côte d’Ivoire-based group to support modernization
item.description: The Cameroonian vegetable oil producer has not named the investor or disclosed the value or structure of the deal announced in Douala.

item.title: Zambia's High Court upholds Kaunda's Lima seat
item.description: Judge Derrick Mulenga dismissed a petition alleging electoral malpractice, intimidation and violence in the August 2026 general election.

item.title: World Bank projects Algeria growth will ease to 3.7% in 2026
item.description: The forecast follows 3.8% growth in 2025, supported by public investment and domestic demand as hydrocarbon revenues fell.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau Olympic secretary-general contests suspension
item.description: Eugénio Lopes says the committee president lacks authority to suspend him and that the order has no effect.

item.title: Morocco tightens African tomato exports as prices fall in Europe
item.description: At Rungis, Moroccan tomatoes now fetch €1.10 to €1.30 per kilogram, down from €1.80 to €2 as shipments rise and sales slow.

item.title: Zambia launches three-month injectable contraceptive
item.description: The Subcutaneous Medogen injection contains 104 milligrams of Medroxyprogesterone Acetate and is intended to widen access to family planning.

item.title: Bubanza peace torch visit shuts market until 16 h 30
item.description: Traders reopened only an hour and a half before the market's usual closing time as schools also stopped lessons for the reception.

item.title: China reaffirms Zambia skills cooperation through training programmes
item.description: Ambassador Han made the pledge at a Lusaka reception where five participants described their training experiences in China.

item.title: Tunisia forecast warns of northern fog and overnight lows of 11°C
item.description: The national meteorological institute expects partly cloudy skies nationwide, with temperatures reaching 17 to 21°C in other regions.

item.title: Kigali to host Africa's Business Heroes finale with $1.5 million in grants
item.description: 10 entrepreneurs selected from more than 24,000 applications will compete in Kigali on December 1–2 for a share of the prize pool.

item.title: CV Interilhas adds new ship to Cabo Verde's inter-island routes
item.description: The operator says the vessel will add capacity, more connections and better comfort for passengers.

item.title: Ramgoolam wants Port-Louis busy after office hours
item.description: Speaking at the Caudan Waterfront's 30th anniversary, Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam said the capital should be a place where Mauritians gather after work.

item.title: Mozambique lawyers’ order opens discipline case against Shamir Mendes
item.description: The order says Mendes is a first-phase trainee, not a registered lawyer, and cannot practise during his first eight months of training.

item.title: UN development programme reviews Sahel project in Ouagadougou
item.description: The 2024-2025 initiative in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger backed youth enterprise, women's economic empowerment and climate resilience.

item.title: Mauritius approves Rs 920 million plan to ease water shortage
item.description: The plan adds transfers from three reservoirs and dams, new 30 m³ tanks, borehole pumps and tanker deliveries to the worst-hit areas.

item.title: Senegal’s under-17s draw 1-1 with Croatia after red card
item.description: Sega Fall Mbodji equalised before half-time in Doha, rescuing a point after Senegal conceded in the eighth minute and lost a player.

item.title: Guinean court jails artist Jack Woumpak for ethnic insult online
item.description: A court in Coyah sentenced him to 24 months, with 18 suspended, after prosecutors had sought three years in prison without suspension.

item.title: Mali's cabinet adopts new rules for private health providers
item.description: The proposed texts replace regulations from 1985 and 1991 to cover newer medical facilities and specialties in the private sector.

item.title: Burkinabè magistrate publishes book on disputes over terminated public contracts
item.description: Ambroise Nébié's 100-page book sets out the remedies open to contractors and how administrative judges decide cases after a public contract is ended.

item.title: Tuareg craft week puts young women’s veil tradition in focus
item.description: At Mali’s National Museum, the event’s third edition has prompted a discussion of when the veil is worn and what it means in Tuareg society.

item.title: UN mission leaves Western Sahara without renewed mandate
item.description: Polisario Front leader Brahim Ghali ordered a general mobilisation on 10 November after an emergency meeting, as ECS Saharaui reported Moroccan troops moving along the wall once.

item.title: Cape Verde sets five new priorities to protect children
item.description: Family Minister Adélsia Almeida announced measures on violence, digital exploitation, case management, children's participation and marriage before 18.

item.title: Burkina Faso and Japan explore deeper cooperation through Japan's aid agency
item.description: Japan's international cooperation agency reported operations in 49 African countries in 2024, with programmes worth 133.3 billion yen, but no new Burkina Faso deal was announced.

item.title: Polisario rejects MINURSO after UN Security Council declines renewal
item.description: At a Madrid conference, its Europe delegate said the mission had failed to deliver the referendum it was created to organise in 1991.

item.title: Morocco sends more officers from its Royal Armed Forces (FAR) to Gaza stabilization force
item.description: The Board of Peace says the officers will reinforce medical operations and logistics planning for the international mission.

item.title: Guinea sets three priorities for youth entrepreneurship and employment
item.description: Education Minister Bintou Keita presented the plan at an entrepreneurship fair in Bamako, including project-based learning and access to public contracts.

item.title: Maroc Telecom finds outdated PHP on 66 sites in cyber scan
item.description: The operator watches its subsidiaries through central security and incident-response teams, with artificial-intelligence agents filtering out false alarms.
